## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Author-anonymised: the journal says reviewers do not know the name of the author; the author must upload a Main Document without identifying information and a separate Title Page, and anonymise citations of their own work (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). Whether reviewers are anonymous to authors is not stated on that page |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. Not stated on the journal's own pages |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Not stated |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank as a number. The journal says manuscripts are generally evaluated by the editor-in-chief and/or by referees, associate editors may take part, and authors may suggest reviewers without binding the editor (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). A secondary summary of an editor's post says the editor aims for three reviewers per paper (https://campanthropology.org/elizabeth-chin-aa-editor-on-the-reviewing-process/, read through a summarising fetch; post date not shown) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | The same editor's post, as summarised, lists reviewer recommendations of revise-and-resubmit, accept or reject, and says the editor does not tally scores (https://campanthropology.org/elizabeth-chin-aa-editor-on-the-reviewing-process/; secondary reading, post date not shown) |

Separately, the repository site https://www.openanthroresearch.org/ returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-23; Wiley says it encourages submission of manuscripts already posted as preprints where journal policy permits, and that authors should keep copyright when posting |

| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Blank | Wiley's sharing chart (a PDF read by text extraction; the chart's layout is not recoverable from the text) says deposit of the accepted version is subject to the embargo listed in the copyright transfer agreement; the agreement for this journal was not read. Embargo: not found |
| Version of Record | Blank | Subscription-article sharing is restricted per the Wiley chart; open-access article (OnlineOpen) can be shared at any time under its Creative Commons licence, per the same chart |

## Format

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research articles (up to 8,000 words); essays (2,000 to 3,000 words); commentaries (up to 1,500 words); interviews (about 2,000 words); review essays (up to 5,000 words, proposal of 500 words); obituaries; single-book reviews (up to 1,000 words, reviewers cannot be students); proposals for online content and multimodal pieces are invited (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | Research articles: up to 8,000 words including all figures, tables, references and notes, but excluding transcriptions and the abstract; initial submissions over 8,000 words will not be considered; an accepted article may be extended to up to 10,500 words at the editors' discretion (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). Note that references count |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Initial limit stated as firm; the 10,500-word extension applies only after acceptance, at the discretion of the associate editors and editor-in-chief (same page) |
| **Abstract limit** | 200 words (same page) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate limit; references count toward the 8,000 words. Citations and references in Chicago author-date style, with DOIs where available; free-format submission is accepted and reformatting happens at copyediting (same page) |
| **Supplementary material** | Not addressed on the journal's page. Figures go in as separate TIF files at 300 dpi or more; tables as Word documents; transcriptions may be submitted outside the word count (same page). Supplementary-file rules are on the Wiley page, which returned 403 |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated. Figures, tables and notes count toward the word limit; each figure needs a caption, alt text and an image description, listed after the references (same page) |

### Orientation

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Both appear. Among the 333 Crossref records of 2021 to 2026 that carry an abstract, "ethnograph-" occurs in 118 (35.4%) and "theory" words in 43 (12.9%); the regexes are in Methodological Preferences. The journal asks for work that makes a novel contribution to or intervention with anthropological theory, method, practice or knowledge production (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Qualitative and interpretive work dominates by keyword: "quantitative / statistical" terms 11 of 333 (3.3%), "survey" 8 (2.4%), against "ethnograph-" 118 (35.4%) and "fieldwork" 52 (15.6%) (Crossref abstracts, counted 2026-11-23; counts are lower bounds because 46.2% of records have an abstract) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The journal states it is a four-field journal (archaeological, biological, sociocultural, linguistic) and strongly encourages work touching all subfields (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). In the abstract sample: "archaeolog-" 38 (11.4%), "linguistic" 17 (5.1%), biological terms 10 (3.0%) |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: Crossref journal-article records published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (721 records, 333 with an abstract = 46.2%; https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0002-7294,from-pub-date:2021-01-01; counts are lower bounds and abstract-based); OpenAlex works (541 articles 2021 to 2026, most-cited list and author-country groups, retrieved 2026-11-23); the journal's own about and submission pages. Keyword regexes are in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries of the 541 OpenAlex articles dated 2021 to 2026 (articles with at least one author in the country; a paper can count for several): United States 354, United Kingdom 50, Canada 43, Australia 16, Germany 15, Netherlands 10, Switzerland 9; Argentina, Hong Kong and Israel 7 each (OpenAlex works group_by authorships.countries, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal says it welcomes contributions from international colleagues and from anthropologists outside the academy (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 34 editorial-board entries on the about page, counted by the country printed in each entry (https://www.americananthropologist.org/about, retrieved 2026-11-23): United States 21, Brazil 2, Canada 2, two entries "Independent Scholar" with no country, two entries with no country printed (one lists "Google", one "University of North Texas"), and one each in India, Portugal, China, South Africa and Mexico (21+2+2+2+2+1+1+1+1+1 = 34). Associate editors: see Identity (18 distinct people) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | The journal's own statements: it has a "World Anthropologies" associate-editor section (two editors, one in Hong Kong and one in the US), a "Multimodal Anthropologies" section and "Public Anthropologies" section, and it encourages land acknowledgments and citation practices that engage scholars and peoples from the research site (https://www.americananthropologist.org/about; https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit). Keyword counts in 333 abstracts: "indigenous" 42 (12.6%); "colonial / decolonial / settler" 59 (17.7%) |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Counts in 333 abstracts: race / racism terms 23 (6.9%); gender / sexuality terms 35 (10.5%); see Sensitive Topics for regexes. The editorial vision asks for an ethics of care in communication and for citational practice that attends to equity (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No single school is named by the journal. Among the OpenAlex most-cited 2021 to 2026 articles (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:0002-7294,publication_year:2021-2026,type:article&sort=cited_by_count:desc, retrieved 2026-11-23) are "Decolonizing US anthropology" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13775, 136 citations), "Knowing Animals: Multispecies Ethnography and the Scope of Anthropology" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13631, 116), "Obstetric Racism" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13559, 84), "Woman the hunter: The archaeological evidence" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13914, 79) and "Objects Don't Have Desires: Toward an Anthropology of Technology beyond Anthropomorphism" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13628, 77). That list mixes decolonial, multispecies, race-critical and archaeological/biological work; it is a citation list, not a statement of editorial leaning |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One stated condition: research articles must make a novel contribution to, or intervention with, anthropological theory, method, practice or knowledge production (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). A summarised post by the editor-in-chief says a paper can be rejected for not articulating a contribution to or intervention with the discipline (https://campanthropology.org/elizabeth-chin-aa-editor-on-the-reviewing-process/; secondary reading, post date not shown).
- **What kind of engagement?** The journal's home page says it looks for articles that are theoretically, methodologically and empirically important and new, and that show how anthropological research improves understanding of issues of cultural significance and practical importance in the present and past (https://www.americananthropologist.org/, retrieved 2026-11-23). It asks that main ideas be comprehensible to nonspecialists and discourages overuse of jargon (same page and https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit). As a four-field journal it strongly encourages material from all subfields, though not as a mechanical exercise.
- **Article types**: research articles up to 8,000 words, essays, commentaries, interviews, review essays, obituaries, book reviews and online content (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Special-section framing**: special sections and Vital Topics Forums are handled by proposal, with papers reviewed individually and, where possible, two reviews per paper plus a third review of the whole section; proposals were not being accepted when read (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). No open call for papers with a deadline was found on the journal's pages.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the journal says "many submissions will be rejected" and that it "is not the right place for everything" (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23, quotes of 5 and 7 words). No source gives a desk-rejection figure (SciRev "n/a": https://scirev.org/journal/american-anthropologist/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Method counts are over the 333 journal-article records of 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 that carry a Crossref abstract (out of 721 journal-article records, 46.2% with abstract; https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0002-7294,from-pub-date:2021-01-01, retrieved 2026-11-23), matching title plus abstract, case-insensitive. In the regexes below, `\|` inside a table cell is a literal alternation bar `|` (escaped only because of the markdown table). Shares use 333 as the denominator; counts are lower bounds. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written mainly for psychology and HCI; where a row does not fit anthropology the cell says so, and rows were added for fieldwork, archival and archaeological or biological work.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 (for quantitative methods generally; no experiments) | Regex `\b(?:quantitative\|statistical\|statistics\|regression\|survey data)\b`: 11 of 333 (3.3%); regex `\bsurveys?\b`: 8 (2.4%). Experimental designs were not counted separately. Biological terms (regex `\b(?:genetic\|genomic\|ancient DNA\|isotop\w*\|skeletal\|bioarchaeolog\w*\|primate\w*)\b`) 10 (3.0%) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Regex `\binterview\w*`: 15 of 333 (4.5%); this includes articles that are themselves interviews with a scholar, so it overstates interviews as a research method; "qualitative" (`\bqualitative\b`) appears in only 2 (0.6%). The row fits poorly: the dominant qualitative mode is ethnography, not named interviews (see next row) |
| Ethnography / fieldwork (added row) | 3 | Regex `\bethnograph\w*`: 118 of 333 (35.4%); regex `\bfield-?work\b\|\bfield research\b`: 52 (15.6%); `\bparticipant[- ]observation\b`: 2 (0.6%). The guidelines also say "We also welcome experimental and multimodal contributions." (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit); they do not tie that sentence to ethnography |
| Autoethnography | 2 | Regex `\bauto-?ethnograph\w*`: 8 of 333 (2.4%); title-only matches in all 721 records: 3 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Regex `\btheor(?:y\|ies\|etical\|ize\|izing\|izations?)\b`: 43 of 333 (12.9%). The journal names theory as one of the four things a research article may contribute to (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) |
| Archival / historical (added row) | 2 | Regex `\barchiv(?:e\|es\|al)\b`: 16 of 333 (4.8%) gives the score. Regex `\bhistor(?:y\|ies\|ical)\b` matches 70 (21.0%, which would score 3), but history words also mark topics rather than methods, so it is not used for the score |
| Archaeological (added row) | 3 | Regex `\barchaeolog\w*\|\barcheolog\w*`: 38 of 333 (11.4%); 41 of all 721 titles match the same regex |
| Linguistic (added row) | 3 | Regex `\blinguistic\b\|\blanguage ideolog\w*\|\bsociolinguistic\w*`: 17 of 333 (5.1%) |
| Multimodal / visual (added row) | 2 | Regex `\b(?:multimodal\|film\|video\|podcast\|photograph\w*\|visual)\b`: 16 of 333 (4.8%); 10 titles of all 721. The journal has a Multimodal Anthropologies editor section (https://www.americananthropologist.org/about) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | Regex `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b`: 0 of 333. One 2026 abstract describes "a mixed methodological approach" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.70136), which the regex does not match |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | Regex `\bmeta-?analy\w*\|\bsystematic review\b`: 0 of 333. The row does not fit the field's usual forms |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Count: of the 333 Crossref abstracts of 2021 to 2026, 235 (70.6%; abstract-only text, title plus abstract gives 237) contain a first-person pronoun by regex `\b(?:I\|my\|me\|we\|our\|us)\b` (case-sensitive; plural "we" and "our" can be a co-author team or generic; Crossref, counted 2026-11-23). Examples: "Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork ... I demonstrate" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.70133), "Our paper takes a mixed methodological approach" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.70136), "the authors consider" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.70139). The guidelines give no rule on first person |
| **Expected density** | Research articles up to 8,000 words including references and notes, an accepted article up to 10,500 (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). Among the 333 abstract-bearing Crossref records, 246 (73.9%) have one author, 53 two, 14 three and 20 four or more (Crossref, counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of 200 words. No keyword requirement was found on the journal's submission page (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Writing style notes** | Plain language is requested: clear writing and straightforward organisation, main ideas comprehensible to nonspecialists, little jargon (https://www.americananthropologist.org/, retrieved 2026-11-23). Word file, 12-point Times New Roman, double spaced, left-justified, endnotes not footnotes, Chicago author-date references with DOIs, free-format first submission; inclusive language is encouraged and a land acknowledgment is encouraged where appropriate; alt text and image descriptions are required for figures (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) |
| **Authorship pattern** | See Expected density: 73.9% single-author among abstract-bearing records (Crossref, 2026-11-23). Records without abstracts include book reviews, which are single-author by nature, so the share among research articles may differ |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Associate-editor entries by heading on the about page: Archaeology 2, Biological Anthropology 1, Cultural Anthropology 5, Linguistic Anthropology 1, Multimodal Anthropologies 3, Public Anthropologies 2, World Anthropologies 2, Book Reviews 1, Obituaries 1, Online Content 1 (2+1+5+1+3+2+2+1+1+1 = 19 entries; the Online Content person is also listed under Cultural Anthropology, so 18 distinct people). Cultural anthropology has the most seats; the board's disciplinary mix is not labelled per member. Reviewer lists are not published | https://www.americananthropologist.org/about, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer list size** | Blank. No reviewer list is published on the journal's pages; the board has 34 entries and the editorial team 1 editor-in-chief, 1 managing editor and 18 distinct associate editors (same page) | https://www.americananthropologist.org/about |
| **Review model** | Reviewers do not know the author's name (author-anonymised); the journal states manuscripts are evaluated by the editor-in-chief and/or referees, with associate editors possibly taking part; authors may suggest reviewers, and the editor is not bound by them | https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report: SciRev has 1 review, which recorded the report quality as 1.0 of 5 and a rejection after 5 reports; one review is not evidence of a pattern (https://scirev.org/reviews/american-anthropologist/); LetPub shows no reviews (reached by search only) | https://scirev.org/journal/american-anthropologist/ |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. The question presupposes a quantitative-leaning pool, which the keyword counts do not suggest (ethnograph- 35.4% against quantitative 3.3%), but how reviewers treat work cannot be read from counts | Crossref counts, see Methodological Preferences |

Board: 34 entries, 21 with United States, 9 in other countries (Brazil 2, Canada 2, India, Portugal, China, South Africa, Mexico), 2 independent scholars, 2 with no country shown (21+9+2+2 = 34) | https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:0002-7294,publication_year:2021-2026,type:article ; https://www.americananthropologist.org/about |

### Sensitive Topics

> Counts are over the 333 Crossref abstract-bearing records of 2021 to 2026 (title plus abstract, case-insensitive; shares use 333; lower bounds). "Receptiveness" cells give frequency only; the one editorial statement found (ethics of care, citation practice, land acknowledgment: https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) is about conduct and does not rate any topic, so no row is rated High.

| Topic Category | Receptiveness | Evidence |
|----------------|---------------|----------|
| Colonialism and decolonization | Frequently published | Regex `\bcolonial\w*\|\bdecoloni\w*\|\bsettler\b`: 59 of 333 (17.7%); title-only 31 of 721. Most-cited 2021 to 2026 article: "Decolonizing US anthropology" (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13775, 136 citations in OpenAlex) |
| Indigenous topics | Frequently published | Regex `\bindigenous\b`: 42 of 333 (12.6%); the journal's guidelines include a land-acknowledgment encouragement for work on Indigenous lands (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit) |
| Violence | Frequently published | Regex `\bviolence\b\|\bviolent\b`: 55 of 333 (16.5%) |
| Gender and sexuality | Present | Regex `\bgender\w*\|\bsexual\w*\|\bqueer\b\|\btrans(?:gender)?\b\|\bLGBT\w*`: 35 of 333 (10.5%); the word-boundary `trans` also matches hyphenated forms such as "trans-Pacific", so this may over-count slightly |
| Race and racism | Present | Regex `\bracism\b\|\bracist\b\|\banti-?black\w*\|\bwhite supremac\w*`: 23 of 333 (6.9%); "Obstetric Racism" is among the most cited (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13559, 84 citations) |
| Religion | Present | Regex `\breligio\w*\|\bChristian\w*\|\bIslam\w*\|\bMuslim\w*`: 29 of 333 (8.7%) |
| Policing, prisons, abolition | Present, smaller | Regex `\bpolic(?:e\|ing)\b\|\bprisons?\b\|\bincarcerat\w*\|\babolition\w*`: 18 of 333 (5.4%) |
| Reproductive politics | Present, smaller | Regex `\babortion\w*\|\breproductive\b`: 10 of 333 (3.0%) |
| Palestine, Gaza, genocide | Rare | Regex `\bPalestin\w*\|\bGaza\b\|\bgenocide\b`: 10 of 333 (3.0%); title-only 10 of 721 |
| AI and technology | Rare in abstracts | Regex `\bartificial intelligence\b\|\bgenerative AI\b\|\bChatGPT\b\|\balgorithm\w*`: 3 of 333 (0.9%); an interview with a scholar of AI and militarism appeared in 2026 (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.70127); "Objects Don't Have Desires" (technology beyond anthropomorphism) is among the most cited (https://doi.org/10.1111/aman.13628, 77 citations) |
| COVID and pandemic | Present, smaller | Regex `\bCOVID\b\|\bpandemic\b`: 10 of 333 (3.0%); title-only 22 of 721 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The journal's own submission page contains no ethics-approval requirement (searched the saved page text for "IRB", "consent" and "ethics approval": only the ethics-of-care and ethical-practices checklist items appear; https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). The publisher requires a statement of prior ethics approval and details on informed consent for research with human participants, and notes that traditional consent forms may not suit all contexts, naming guidance on partnering with Indigenous peoples (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the majority: 246 of 333 (73.9%) abstract-bearing Crossref records have one author (counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The journal states it welcomes work by anthropologists outside the academy (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23); 2 of the 34 board entries and 1 of 18 associate editors are listed as independent scholars (https://www.americananthropologist.org/about); the journal does not charge for submission or publication (same submission page). Wiley requires an ORCID for American Anthropological Association journals (same page) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal's own page states none (searched the saved page text for "data availability": not present). Wiley's policy says all research published in its journals must include a Data Availability Statement, with an explanation where data cannot be shared (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Reviewers are told not to expect the author's name; the Main Document must carry no identifying information and own-work citations are replaced with "Author", with those references left out of the reference list (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23). A manuscript already posted as a preprint, for example in the Association's repository, is identifiable by search |
| **AI use** | Allowed with disclosure under Wiley's policy; AI cannot be an author (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html, retrieved 2026-11-23); see AI Policy |
| **Open access and cost** | No author fee on the subscription route; OnlineOpen is an optional paid route (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23); APC USD 3750 per Wiley's price list (https://authorservices.wiley.com/asset/Wiley-Journal-APCs-OnlineOpen.xlsx, updated 12 October 2026, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Platform change** | All new manuscripts since 15 April 2025 go through the Wiley Research Exchange platform; earlier submissions stay in ScholarOne (https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: initial submissions over 8,000 words, with references, notes and figures counted, will not be considered (Format; https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit).
- **Anonymisation**: the Main Document must be free of identifying information, with own-work citations rewritten as "Author" and omitted from the reference list (Peer Review; same page).
- **Contribution**: research articles are expected to make a novel contribution to or intervention with anthropological theory, method, practice or knowledge production (Framing Requirements; same page).
- **AI use**: undisclosed substantive AI use breaches the Wiley policy (AI Policy; https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; ethics-approval wording on the journal's own page is absent, and Wiley's general rule applies (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no publisher turnaround figure was read; the one SciRev report shows 13 weeks to a rejection after 5 reports (Review Cycle Time; n=1).
- **Accessibility work**: every figure and table needs a caption, alt text and an image description supplied at the end of the manuscript (Format; same page).
- **Word budget**: references and notes count within 8,000 words, which is tight for note-heavy or multi-site ethnography (Format; the claim about note-heavy work is an inference from the stated counting rule, not a reported experience).
- **Open access**: the optional OnlineOpen route carries an APC, listed at USD 3750 on Wiley's price list of 12 October 2026 (Open Access).

### Best Suited For

- Sociocultural, linguistic, archaeological or biological work framed so that nonspecialists across subfields can follow the argument: the journal names all four fields and asks for comprehensible main ideas (Framing Requirements; https://www.americananthropologist.org/).
- Ethnographic and historical-archival research with a clear theoretical intervention: "ethnograph-" 35.4%, history terms 21.0%, theory terms 12.9% of 333 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Decolonial, Indigenous, race-critical and multispecies-style work: colonial terms 17.7%, Indigenous 12.6%, and the most-cited 2021 to 2026 articles are on these themes (Sensitive Topics; Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Short forms for authors who are not writing a full article: essays (2,000 to 3,000 words), commentaries and interviews are listed article types (Format).
- Authors outside the academy: the journal says it welcomes them (Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Quantitative, experimental or systematic-review designs presented without an anthropological argument: quantitative terms appear in 3.3% and meta-analysis or systematic-review terms in 0 of 333 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). This reflects frequency, not a stated exclusion.
- Specialist site reports or narrowly technical work with no argument for a broad readership: the journal asks for comprehensible main ideas and says it is not the right place for everything (Framing Requirements; https://www.americananthropologist.org/how-to-submit). The book-review FAQ separately lists "a site report" as an example of a book too specific for the journal; that is about books, not articles.
- Manuscripts over 8,000 words with no plan to cut (Hard Blockers).
- Anyone needing a firm turnaround time: none is published (Review Cycle Time).
